images.title: 1345 in fives needs 269 symbols
images.purpose: Shows that writing 1345 with only a symbol for five needs 269 copies of that symbol, far too many.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. One long row of identical small squares running almost the full width, broken by three dots, with one brace underneath counting them.
images.exact_structure: At the left, the large dark label 1345 followed by a dark equals sign. Then a single row of identical small amber (#E69F00) squares: exactly 12 squares, then three grey (#6B7280) dots, then exactly 3 more squares. Under the whole row of squares, one long teal (#0072B2) brace labelled 269 squares. Above the first square, a small key: one amber square with the grey label 5 beside it. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: With only one group size, a large number needs far too many symbols.
images.description: Shows that writing 1345 with only a symbol for five needs 269 copies of that symbol, far too many.

image_decisions.why: The long row of identical symbols makes the limit of a single group size felt at a glance.
